versions.localizedDescription:
Sevbify 5.0.0-beta.45

## What's new in beta.45 (Android)

From your Bad Friends log: the stream link was refused again (a 12 s wait, then my retry fixed it), and the video then failed with `ERROR_CODE_IO_NETWORK_CONNECTION_FAILED` after 22 s.

- **A refused link is caught before you wait on it.** Right before a YouTube stream goes to the player, the app asks for its first bytes the way the player does (Python's check can differ from the player's network stack). If YouTube answers 4xx, the link is replaced by a fresh one from the next client, up to twice. The log shows `link check: HTTP 200 (N ms)`.
- **The Playback status log says more about failures**: the HTTP status code (`ERROR … (HTTP 403)`), and, when a stream can't connect or is refused, how the phone's network reaches that YouTube server (`network to …: IPv6 ok 40 ms, IPv4 no answer 3000 ms`; no addresses are shown). The log keeps the last 24 lines instead of 16. If the waits come from the connection (for example IPv6 not working on your Wi-Fi), that line will show it.

### Earlier, in beta.44 (Android)

From your log (`ERROR_CODE_IO_BAD_HTTP_STATUS` right after "play … googlevideo.com"): YouTube was refusing the audio link, so the player gave up and moved to the next song. The quick YouTube client added in beta.39 can hand out a link that extracts fine but is refused when played, which is why online songs (and ad-free episodes) skipped while your own library played.

- **Links are tested before they're used.** After a quick client gives a link, the app asks for its first two bytes; if YouTube refuses, the next client is tried (the last one is always used as it is). This applies to songs and to podcast episode audio and video.
- **If the player is refused anyway**, the app drops that link, moves to the next YouTube client and asks for a fresh link, once (the log says `link refused: asking for a new one`).
- **Episodes whose YouTube title differs from the feed's title are found more often.** Once a show's own channel is known (learned the first time any of its episodes matches), the episode is looked for among that channel's recent videos by title and by length: a video of the same length (within 8%) that shares some words with the title is accepted when it is clearly the best of those. Nothing is guessed when two videos fit equally.

### Earlier, in beta.43 (Android)

Podcast video fixes (from your Fin vs History recording, where Watch video found nothing and the Video tab was still waiting after half a minute):

- **Faster episode audio and video links.** Songs got a quick YouTube client in beta.39, but podcast episodes (the ad-free version and the Video tab) were still asking YouTube the slow way. They now try the quick client first and fall back to the full list, like songs. YouTube's answer for an episode is also kept for 10 minutes and shared, so listening then tapping Video (or going back to Audio) doesn't ask YouTube twice.
- **Watch video on a show page finds more.** When no channel is named like the show, it used to look for the channel of only the newest episode's video, which is often not on YouTube yet (your newest episode was 2 days old). It now tries up to four recent episodes, and it remembers the show's channel as soon as any episode's video is found (playing it ad-free counts), so the button then opens the channel straight away.
- **The Playback status log shows how long each step took**: `video lookup (N s)`, `ad-free audio link (N s)`, `video link (N s)`.

### Earlier, in beta.42 (Android)

Falling back after beta.40/41, where streamed songs were found but sat at 0:00 and skipped on (your genre and artist-search recordings):

- **Streaming is back to how it worked in beta.39.** The two beta.40/41 changes that touch the streamed audio itself are now switches in Settings → Playback, **off by default**: *Gapless songs (experimental)* and *Audio cache (experimental)*.
